fields.Name: Wheelchair Accessible - Instructor Area/Front of Room
Assistive Listening System - Self-Serve Mobile App

fields.Definition: Microphone(s) available in room can be either Wireless Handheld, Wireless Lapel or Audience Microphones.
Room is not wheelchair accessible due to stairs/steps and no alternate route.

Any space students use outside of scheduled classes to study or socialize. They can be anything from a café in the Nest, to a silent study space in the library. Informal Learning Spaces are found across campus in many different buildings. For a list of informal learning spaces, visit the Informal Learning Spaces page.
Used for projecting video presentation material from a computer or document camera.
Window(s) and/or skylight(s) located in room.

Typically a microphone with a button to activate/de-activate; used for voice amplification, located on the student desks for interaction with instructors, other students, or remote participants using video-conferencing or streaming capabilities.
Large flat panel display facing the presenter. Displays the same video signal that is selected to show on the main display behind the presenter (computer or document camera.)
Access to food or drink vendors nearby. Hours of vendors vary.
The accessible path to the front of the room requires the use of an incline platform lift to traverse stairs/steps.
Allows wireless sharing of your screen from a Mac or Windows laptop onto room display(s).

fields.Term: Instructor Area/Front of Room Not Wheelchair Accessible
fields.Definition: Room is not wheelchair accessible due to stairs/steps and no alternate route.
The accessible path to the room or the front of the room requires the use of a vertical platform lift.
A video camera enabled device used for presenting pre-printed images, items, or writing to be projected via a multimedia projector.
At least some seats in the room are wheelchair accessible; if the room is tiered, there is an accessible path to some student seats.
This type of input is used to connect your laptop, iPad, or newer digital devices to the AV presentation system. This is a digital connection.
No entrances to the classroom have a powered door (door that opens by pushing a button or using a touchless sensor.)
High-tech group work rooms where each pod has its own display. Presentations can be shared to any/all displays from the instructor lectern or student pods.
Instructor writing surface in the room is chalkboard(s). Chalk and erasers are provided.
Used for voice amplification, either held in your hand or placed on a microphone stand.

fields.Term: Assistive Listening System - Self-Serve Mobile App
fields.Definition: Streams live audio over a wireless network directly to users’ smartphones, allowing users to listen in real time through headphones, hearing aids, or cochlear implants. To use this system, download the Sennheiser MobileConnect app, connect to the ubcsecure Wireless Network, and scan the QR code that is posted on the wall in the classroom to connect to the channel.
Used for voice amplification, comes with a clip to attach the small microphone to your lapel.
Power outlets are available at 100% of student seats.
Designated for quiet individual study. Campus libraries, reading rooms and study carrels typically offer silent study space.

fields.Term: Wheelchair Accessible - Instructor Area/Front of Room
fields.Definition: The front of the room is wheelchair accessible; if the room is tiered, there is an accessible path to the instructor area.
Different content can be projected on two or more screens through the AV presentation system. For example, a laptop on one screen and a document camera on another.
Spaces designed to support individual study. Noise and activity levels will vary by space.
Writing surfaces available in room can be either whiteboards, chalkboards or glassboards.

A Windows PC computer system is available at the instructor station. Comes installed with Microsoft PowerPoint, Word, and Excel. Internet access requires a UBC campus-wide login (CWL). For more information please visit http://www.cwl.ubc.ca.
Meets Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies’ requirements for off-site Final Doctoral Oral Examinations.
Allows users to interact with the room PC via touch capability on the flat panel display. Also allows notes to be handwritten on the screen and saved to the room PC.
At least one entrance to the classroom has a powered door that opens by pushing a button or using a touchless sensor.
Instructor writing surface in the room is whiteboard(s) or glassboard(s). Instructors and students are responsible for supplying their own dry-erase markers; erasers are provided.

Streams live audio to a portable receiver, allowing users to listen in real time through headphones, hearing aids, or cochlear implants. To use this system, email AV.support@ubc.ca to borrow a receiver.
Spaces designed to support group study or group work. Furniture is typically designed to support collaborative activities.

An audience response system that can be used for polls and quizzes. iClicker is now the iClicker Cloud, and no special device or hardware is required to use it. For more information please visit the Learning Technology Hub webpage: https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/iclicker-cloud-instructor-guide/.

Involves some combination of in-person and online learning, with the goals of increasing flexibility in terms of when and where students learn, and taking advantage of in-person and online spaces and learning technologies to enhance student learning. Three common components of this learning style are online learning materials and activities, in-person activities in the classroom guided by instructors, and structured independent study for students.
Video camera enabled devices used for presenting pre-printed images, items, or  writing to be projected via a multimedia projector.
A Plasma or LCD/LED screen that is used for AV presentations.
A type of blended learning in which students engage with content or materials prior to the start of class so as to allow more time in the classroom for active learning activities and discussion.
Allows the recording of a video camera feed, audio, and presentation materials for later viewing and distribution or live streaming.

When students are physically distributed at multiple sites but need to learn at the same time. The UBC School of Medicine, for example, uses this model. This type of learning provides more flexibility and opportunity for students to learn beyond the traditional classroom setting.
Power outlets are available at approximately 50% of student seats.
Inputs offered in room can be either Auxiliary video with Audio, HDMI, or Laptop VGA with Audio inputs.

Learning spaces specifically designed to support student-centered, flexible, and interactive learning. Active Learning Classrooms contain furniture designed for collaboration, and both peer-to-peer learning and instructor-student interaction. High-tech Active Learning Classrooms may feature technology that allows both instructors and students to share their work with the class.

This
  type of input is used to connect your laptop, iPad, or newer digital devices
  to the AV presentation system. This is a digital connection.

Real-time communication tool that enables instructors and students in different locations to interact through live video, audio, chat and content sharing. It supports synchronous hybrid teaching and learning, where some participants are physically present in the classroom while others join remotely.
